clue.text: Artist wins election in town

parts.note: a party that wins an election in a seat is said to gain it, so this phrase gives gains
a borough is a town with its own corporation

explanation.surface: A painter triumphs at the polls in his home town.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'wins election in town' as 'gains borough', the language of election-night results; Thomas Gainsborough was the 18th-century English portrait and landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gainsborough was a celebrated English painter, so he is an example of the category.

clue.text: Team up

parts.note: read literally, a team that is up in the sky: those who staff a flight

explanation.definitionFit: An aircrew is the group of people who fly and staff an aeroplane, airborne while working.

clue.text: Unnecessary indicators on top of stereo

parts.note: needles are the pointers on dials and gauges

indicators.note: top of says take the first letter of stereo

explanation.surface: Pointless dials perched on a hi-fi system.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on' places NEEDLES above the S taken by 'top of' from 'stereo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless means not required, superfluous.

clue.text: Barks of trees?

definitions.meaning: barks as a verb: the howls of hounds
laurels whose leaves are used in cooking

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests tree bark; the question mark flags the dog sense of 'barks'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogs bay when they bark loudly, and bays are laurel trees with aromatic leaves.

clue.text: An eccentric breeds rats or birds

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A strange person raises either vermin or birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' looks like a noun for an odd person but signals the anagram of BREEDS RATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Redbreasts is a traditional name for robins, songbirds with orange-red chests.

clue.text: Haul collected by Pole Prussian lancer

indicators.note: collected means gathered up, so the letters are gathered into a new order

parts.note: N is the North Pole

explanation.surface: A Polish cavalryman gathers up loot for a Prussian lancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person but gives N, the North Pole. Uhlans were lance-armed light cavalry, originally Polish.
explanation.definitionFit: Uhlans were light cavalry armed with lances, serving in the Prussian army.

clue.text: Element discovered humanoid initially, one in human form

indicators.note: initially says take the first letter of humanoid
in says the one-letter piece sits inside the shuffled letters
form as a noun means shape, so the letters of human are put into a new shape

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A newly found element is said to have revealed a manlike creature in human shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' reshapes HUMAN into AHNUM, 'in' puts I inside it, and 'initially' gives H. Hahnium was a proposed name for element 105, after Otto Hahn.
explanation.definitionFit: Hahnium was a proposed name for a synthetic chemical element, number 105, now dubnium.

clue.text: Coal found in dark red suit

parts.note: black means dark
diamonds is one of the two red suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Fuel turned up in a crimson outfit of dark colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red suit' is clothing on the surface but a suit of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Black diamonds is a nickname for coal, valuable dark fuel.

clue.text: Turning up in Antwerp without sign on special occasions

indicators.note: without means outside, so the city name goes round the reversed letters

parts.note: Anvers is the French name for Antwerp

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue says the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Arriving in a Belgian city without any signal, on festive days.
explanation.walkthrough: Anvers is the French name for Antwerp, which a solver may not know; 'without' means outside here, not lacking, and 'on' stacks the pieces in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Anniversaries are dates marking a past event each year, celebrated days.

clue.text: Crook nearly caught breaking in — that's a crime

indicators.note: breaking in says one piece forces its way inside the other
crook as a verb means bend out of shape, so the letters of nearly are bent into a new order

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A villain is almost nabbed during a burglary, which is of course an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' looks like the criminal but is the anagram signal: NEARLY becomes LARENY, and 'breaking in' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is the legal term for theft, a specific offence.

clue.text: Swimmer causing row about original Plymouth boundaries?

indicators.note: about means the noise word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a row is a loud noise, a din

indicators.note: the boundaries of a word are its first and last letters, taken here from both original and Plymouth

explanation.surface: A swimmer sparks a dispute over where the old city limits of Plymouth lay.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks you to think of a town's borders, but 'boundaries' means the outer letters of the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolphin is a sea mammal that swims, so it is a swimmer.

clue.text: Song from coral at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tune drawn from a reef out in the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A carol is a festive hymn, a kind of song.

clue.text: Endless salt water I'd taken back to South Island seaport

indicators.note: endless says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: brine is salt water

indicators.note: taken back says these letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: taken as written, I and D
SI is an abbreviation for South Island, as in New Zealand

explanation.surface: Seawater I'd carried home to an island in the south, from a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts BRINE to BRIN, and 'taken back' turns ID into DI. Brindisi is a port in the heel of Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Brindisi is a harbour city on the Adriatic coast of Italy, an example of a port.

clue.text: Cause fight after graduate snatches some jewellery

indicators.note: after says the fight piece comes after the rest
snatches says the graduate grabs and holds the jewellery inside

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
a ring is an item of jewellery
a bout is a contest or fight

explanation.surface: Start a brawl after a student grabs some jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cause' is a verb here; BA, a Bachelor of Arts, is the usual crossword graduate.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring about is to make happen, to produce as a result.

clue.text: Mate drowns at sea, going with the current

indicators.note: at sea means in confusion, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A ship's officer drowns in the ocean, swept along by the tide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' fits the drowning picture, but it is the anagram signal for MATE plus DROWNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving in the same direction as a river's flow is travelling with the stream, toward its mouth.

clue.text: Pirate taking part in pirates' meeting

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A buccaneer attends a gathering of his fellow sea robbers.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'pirateS MEEting'. Smee is Captain Hook's boatswain in Peter Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Smee is Captain Hook's sidekick in Peter Pan, a fictional buccaneer.

clue.text: Part of French battle

parts.note: action is military fighting, a battle

explanation.surface: A piece of a French combat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraction is a portion of a whole.

clue.text: Walton loses points as a singer

indicators.note: loses says letters are removed from the name

parts.note: W and N are compass points, west and north

explanation.surface: The composer William Walton is docked marks, as a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' are compass points: take W and N out of WALTON. Walton suggests the composer, a natural false trail for a music clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a voice with a low female or high male range, and so a kind of vocalist.

clue.text: Glorious day and night for play

definitions.meaning: the Glorious ..., 12 August, when British grouse shooting opens
... Night, a Shakespeare comedy named after the eve of Epiphany

explanation.walkthrough: The 'Glorious Twelfth' is the British start of the grouse season, 12 August.
explanation.definitionFit: The Glorious Twelfth is 12 August, start of grouse shooting in Britain, and Twelfth Night is Shakespeare's comedy, named for an evening.

clue.text: Investments one has confidence in?

parts.note: a unit is one single thing
trusts means has confidence in

explanation.surface: Asks whether a certain person's funds are placed in someone they believe in.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'one has confidence in' is read literally, as a single thing that believes.
explanation.definitionFit: Unit trusts are pooled funds sold in shares, a British form of collective investment like a mutual fund.

clue.text: Duck observed on poster

parts.note: saw means observed
a bill is a poster stuck up on a wall

explanation.surface: Someone stoops to avoid being seen on a billboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like a verb but is the bird; 'on' places SAW above BILL in the down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The sawbill is a nickname for the merganser, a fish-eating bird with a serrated beak.

clue.text: Composing love poetry while in foreign lands

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
verse is poetry
as can mean while

explanation.surface: Writing romantic poems while travelling abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composing' is a link word here, introducing the pieces; love = O comes from tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Overseas means abroad, beyond the sea in other countries.

clue.text: Hose blows

definitions.meaning: punches, as in a sock on the jaw

explanation.definitionFit: Hose is a term for stockings or other legwear, and to sock someone is to punch them, so socks are punches.

clue.text: Neat eater ate plucked quail

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so a cow

indicators.note: plucked says letters are pulled out, here the word ate from eater

explanation.surface: A tidy diner consumes a game bird stripped of its feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' is the archaic word for cattle, not 'tidy'; 'quail' is the verb, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To quail is to shrink back in fear, to cringe.

clue.text: Revolutionary article about China's capital is genuine

indicators.note: about says the reversed word goes round the letter
revolutionary means turning over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: capital means the first letter of China's

explanation.surface: A rebel's essay on the Chinese capital is authentic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' turns THE into EHT, which goes 'about' C, the capital (first letter) of China. Echt is German for real, used in English.
explanation.definitionFit: Echt, borrowed from German, means authentic or typical.

clue.text: Actually, an author's unfinished work is included

indicators.note: is included says the next piece goes inside
unfinished says the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Daniel Defoe was the author of Robinson Crusoe
an act is a deed or piece of work

explanation.surface: In truth, a writer's incomplete manuscript is part of the collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts DEFOE to DEFO, and ACT 'is included' in it.
explanation.definitionFit: De facto is Latin for 'in fact', existing in reality whatever the law says.

clue.text: What's cooking? Copper is, in midfield

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
the middle of the word field is its central letter E

explanation.surface: Asks what is happening, then says a policeman is standing in the centre of the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the element; 'mid' takes the centre letter E of FIELD.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuisine is a style of food preparation, literally what a kitchen produces.

clue.text: Get in hastily somehow without haste

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: A command to climb in quickly, done in some fashion, slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges GET IN HASTILY; the definition contradicts the hurry of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting hesitatingly means pausing and holding back, so not rushing.
